title: Add Graceful Shutdown Handling for Production Stability
description: Implements a zero‑dependency graceful shutdown system that intercepts SIGTERM, SIGINT, uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections. It stops accepting new connections, waits for in‑flight requests to finish, and then exits cleanly, preventing data loss and improving container orchestration reliability.
testCases: Start the yantraverse server, issue a long‑running request, trigger SIGTERM and verify the server stops accepting new connections while the in‑flight request completes before the process exits
Trigger an uncaughtException while the server is idle and ensure the graceful shutdown sequence runs, logs the error, and exits with code 1
acceptance: When a termination signal or fatal error occurs, the framework must (1) stop accepting new HTTP connections within 100 ms, (2) allow all active requests to finish up to a configurable timeout (default 5 s), (3) close the underlying HTTP server, (4) flush any pending logs, and (5) exit the process with the appropriate exit code (0 for SIGTERM/SIGINT, 1 for uncaught errors). All tests must pass and no resource leaks should be detected.
reason: Containers and serverless platforms rely on graceful termination to avoid dropped requests and corrupted state. Adding this feature directly addresses production reliability concerns, aligns with the recent stability focus, and requires minimal code while delivering high business value.
